---
title: "Overview"
---

This book is the narrative companion to `scripts/`. Computation stays
in the scripts; the chapters are theory, design, and criticism of how
those scripts should be run.

The scientific target is DeCovarT's cell-type Gaussians: sparse
precisions $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}\equiv\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}^{-1}$ and means
$\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}$, estimated from labelled single-cell
transcriptomes and plugged into the bulk convolution. Indices follow
the article Methods: gene $g=1,\ldots,G$, cell type $j=1,\ldots,J$,
sample $i=1,\ldots,N$.

The planned Suppinger benchmark is a **$3\times 2\times 2$** product,
not a single pipeline. Three undirected GGM families, two lifts from
cells to a population Gaussian, and two gene-panel strategies (the naive
screen alone, or that screen plus an optional stricter Pareto
refinement). That is 12 routes. The aim is to see **which steps move
deconvolution**, not to retain every cell of the product in the paper.
Bures–Wasserstein alignment and sparse-plus-low-rank GGMs stay
**perspectives**; they are not factors in @fig-pipeline.

```{mermaid}

  P --> D
```

Reading order puts the **naive** screen before GRN inference, and the
**optional** genetic algorithm after the graphs, because the second
objective needs $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}$. Deconvolution comparators,
the early-versus-standard Wnt reading, and sensitivity analyses close
the book.
